result.stdout:
cascade watch — Start hot reload file watcher

Usage: cascade watch [options]
       cascade run --watch [options]

Options:
  -p, --project <path>       Path to .csproj (auto-detected if omitted)
  --component <name>         Isolate a single component for preview
  --theme <name>             Override theme (e.g. FluentTheme)
  --mode <mode>              Override mode: Light, Dark, System
  --size <preset|WxH>        Window size: compact, medium, expanded, large, or WxH
  --mock                     Generate mock data for FetchAsync calls
  --no-hot-reload            Disable hot reload (just build and run)
  --help, -h                 Show this help

Size presets:
  compact    500x800
  medium     768x1024
  expanded   1024x768   (default)
  large      1440x900

Hot reload:
  Changes to .cs files trigger Roslyn incremental compilation.
  Method body edits are applied via Edit-and-Continue deltas
  in < 700ms without losing component state.
  Structural changes (new fields, type changes) trigger a full rebuild,
  which kills the running app process, rebuilds, relaunches, and
  re-acquires the hot-reload pipe automatically.

Performance target: < 700ms from save to visual update.

cascade doctor — Run comprehensive project diagnostics

Usage: cascade doctor [options]

Options:
  --format <text|json>      Output format (default: text)
  --fail-on <severity>      Exit code threshold: error (default), warning, info
  --category <name>         Run only named category (repeatable)
  --help, -h                Show this help

Categories:
  accessibility    Missing labels, contrast violations, focus order
  layout           Overflow, missing constraints, ambiguous sizing
  performance      Excessive re-renders, expensive intrinsic queries
  localization     Missing keys, unused keys, format mismatches
  storage          Duplicate keys, reserved prefix, unserializable types
  theme            Low contrast tokens, missing required overrides
  reactivity       Signal writes in Render(), unused signals

Examples:
  cascade doctor --fail-on warning
  cascade doctor --category accessibility --category theme
  cascade doctor --format json --fail-on warning

Use --format json for AI-agent-friendly output.

result.stdout:
Usage: cascade package [options]

Options:
  --project, -p <path>         Project to package
  --platform <os>              Target platform (win, mac, linux)
  --arch <arch>                Architecture (x64, arm64, universal)
  --formats <list>             Comma-separated formats (e.g., deb,rpm,appimage)
  --output, -o <dir>           Output directory (default: ./dist)
  --configuration, -c <name>   Build configuration (default: Release)
  --framework-dependent        Don't self-contain the runtime
  --installer                  Build a one-file installer from the app's [Installer] class
                               (NativeAOT by default: smaller, native, no JIT)
  --no-aot                     With --installer: self-contained JIT build (no C++ toolchain needed)
  --keep-locales               With --installer: keep ICU per-culture locale satellites

Installer signing (Authenticode; signs the wizard, uninstaller, and launcher):
  --self-sign "<name>"         Generate a throwaway code-signing cert on the fly.
                               Nothing to install/manage — just give a name, e.g.
                                 cascade package --installer --self-sign "Adam Marciniec"
  --sign-cert <thumb|.pfx>     Use an existing cert: a 40-char cert-store SHA-1 thumbprint,
                               or a path to a .pfx file (add --sign-password if it has one).
  --sign-password <pwd>        Password for a .pfx passed to --sign-cert.
  --sign-timestamp <url>       RFC-3161 timestamp server (default: DigiCert).
    Requires signtool.exe (Windows SDK; auto-located). NOTE: a self-signed cert does
    NOT stop end-user SmartScreen/AV warnings — only a real OV/EV cert builds reputation.

  -h, --help                   Show this help

result.stdout:
Usage: cascade mcp serve [--app <name>]

Run the long-lived stdio MCP bridge — the server an MCP client (e.g.
Claude Code) connects to. It speaks MCP over stdin/stdout, discovers
running Cascade apps via the shared registry, and forwards live tool
calls to them. With no app running it still serves tool schemas and
returns structured "no live instance" errors. Without --app it targets
whichever Cascade app is running.

Usage: cascade mcp inspect <node_id> [--app <name>]

Get complete details on a specific UI node including source location, bounds, theme tokens, accessibility info, reactive signals, and render statistics. Use cascade_tree first to find the node ID.

Usage: cascade mcp whodrew <x> <y> [--app <name>]

Answer "what drew the pixel at (x, y)?" — returns every draw from the last presented frame touching that pixel, in paint order: shape ops (kind, bounds, colors), image blits, and glyph quads (glyph id, font size, atlas rect), each with the DevTools node id that emitted it. The first call enables draw capture and repaints once. Source locations are not included (node-to-source mapping is not implemented yet); use the node id with cascade_inspect_node.

Usage: cascade mcp instances [--rect <value>] [--limit <value>] [--app <name>]

List the glyph quads the GPU drew in the last presented frame, optionally filtered to a screen rect: device position/size, glyph id, font size, atlas texel rect, color, clip, and the emitting node id.   --rect               __rect (String)
  --limit              limit (Int)

  --rect x,y,w,h   Only glyphs overlapping this device-pixel rect
  --limit N        Max instances returned (default 200)

Each instance reports its atlas texel rect — pass it to
'cascade mcp atlas --region u,v,w,h' to see the actual bitmap.

Usage: cascade mcp focus <node_id> [--wait-frames <value>] [--app <name>]

Simulate user interaction: hover, click, press, release, focus, blur, right_click, drag. For drag: use start_x/start_y (node-relative), delta_x/delta_y or end_x/end_y, and steps. Use x/y to click at specific coordinates (e.g. overlay popups); they are in the returned screenshot's pixel space by default, so a point read off a screenshot can be clicked directly (coord_space="logical" for raw logical coordinates). Frame-synchronous: the response includes presented_frame and timed_out — timed_out=true means nothing repainted within ~2s (no sleep needed before screenshots).

Arguments:
  <node_id>  (String)

Options:
  --wait-frames        wait_frames (Int)
